messages:
anika_p: quick perf dump from today's nightly runs — KV cache hit-rate is steady but p99 token latency regressed ~22% on 8xA100 TP=4, PP=2 configs after the kernel bump. attaching the condensed profile.

cheng_wu: can you paste the profile snippet? wondering if all-reduce / comm overlap is worse or if compute kernels regressed.

anika_p: pasted snippet below (from perf-trace, condensed):
```
stage    | compute(ms) | comm(ms) | comm% | notes
encode   | 12          | 3        | 20%   | small, ok
attn_kv  | 26          | 46       | 64%   | allreduce-heavy on TP dims
ffn      | 34          | 8        | 19%   | kernel time up a bit
kv_serv  | 8           | 2        | 20%   | hit-rate steady
overall  | 80          | 59       | 42%   | p99 dominated by attn_kv comm
```

eli: ouch — that attn_kv line screams cross-rank allreduce hotpath. if KV shards are stripe-distributed across TP ranks we're hitting N*N allreduces per layer.

alex_k: i'm seeing similar in my local repro. after the kernel bump we flipped a kernel variant that removed async memcpy->nccl overlap for the sharded gather. likely fallout: less comm/compute overlap.

mari: i actually rolled that kernel change — the fused path that tried to lower memory usage now forces synchronous nccl calls in the hot loop. i can revert and run garden run.

anika_p: thanks. in parallel i sketched a mapping idea: 'layer-local shards' where KV for adjacent layers are co-located on the same TP group to reduce cross-group allreduces, and hot key mini-replication for top-K heavy tokens. tradeoffs: slightly more memory, but reduces allreduce fanout and allows better overlap.

cheng_wu: that maps toward a hybrid TP/DP strategy. if we replicate hot keys across DP groups (replication factor r), we convert some allreduces into local reads. math: comm_cost ~ O(shard_count * layer_count) -> becomes O(shard_count/r) for hot keys. worth prototyping.

alex_k: also consider batching heuristics: increase microbatch from 4->8 to amortize per-request allreduce overhead, but watch KV prefetch pressure. i have a quick config diff:
```yaml
kvcache_shard_strategy: "hybrid-locality-v1"
hot_key_replication: 2
microbatch_size: 8
kernel_fallback_policy: "prefer-async-over-sync"
```

eli: +1 on fallback policy — we need a runtime feature that selects kernel variant based on measured overlap. i can add an experiment flag to toggle the old async path per-model.

mari: i'm running a revert + garden run now (ops-bot will post results). if that restores overlap then we know the kernel change caused the regression.

ops-bot: garden run started (run id g-2026-03-18-047). notify: will post perf summary when complete.

anika_p: if revert helps, next steps: 1) temporary revert in canary and run long-tail evals, 2) prototype hybrid-locality shard mapping in simulator and run microbench, 3) tune microbatch and prefetch thresholds (suggested heuristics: prefer larger microbatch when attn_kv comm% > 35% and kv hit-rate > 0.6).

cheng_wu: i'll take step 2, sim harness already supports mapping function input. alex_k please add the kernel-variant toggle flag (step 1) so canary can be quick. mari ty for running revert.

alex_k: will do. quick note: if we implement hot-key replication, need eviction/inv-sync logic to avoid stale KV states across replicas. that adds complexity to rollout.

anika_p: true — for initial prototype keep replication for read-only hot entries (short TTL) to avoid consistency headaches.

eli: ok assigning: mari -> revert + garden run, alex_k -> kernel toggle flag + canary rollout, cheng_wu -> shard-mapping sim + perf bench, anika_p -> adjust batching heuristics and collect p50/p90/p99 after runs. i'll monitor.

mari: started job, ETA ~12m.

ops-bot: garden run g-2026-03-18-047 completed. summary: p99 latency improved ~18% vs bumped-kernel, allreduce time reduced on attn_kv by ~40% (measured). more detailed trace uploaded to infra/perf/g-2026-03-18-047.

anika_p: great — looks like kernel path was main culprit. still want the hybrid mapping prototype to reduce base comm for larger models. cheng, when sim results land ping here.

cheng_wu: will post sim results in ~2h. initial sim shows hybrid-locality reduces expected allreduce volume by ~30% for encoder-heavy models, cost of ~8% extra KV memory.

alex_k: added kernel toggle to runtime (flag --prefer-async-kvcopy). will flip in canary tomorrow morning.

anika_p: thanks team. filing a short follow-up doc in /docs/perf/ after we validate canary. actions captured. :thumbsup:
